note: Every Live series card of MLB The Show 20 (the roster of each MLB club at the edition's last roster update) as ShowZone keeps it, as [uuid, name, team, position, secondary positions, overall, born]. "born" is a US state or a country, "" where ShowZone names none (8 cards). Written by npm run import:mlb-showzone from ShowZone's cached answers; read by npm run build:mlb-seasons.

source.name: MLB The Show 20 Live series
source.provenance: Sony's own API for this edition is gone. ShowZone (showzone.gg), a fan-run card database that is not the publisher, keeps every Live card of the edition at its last roster update and serves them from a public data API (data.showzone.gg), read once on 2026-11-08: 74 pages of 100 cards, MLB The Show 18 to 21. showzone.gg's robots.txt disallows /api on its own host; the data host serves no robots.txt. ShowZone states 'All Rights Reserved' and publishes no terms; as with Sony's own data, the rights are not cleared. Its MLB The Show 21 equals Sony's own API (scripts/data/mlb-the-show-21.json) on all 2,092 cards, uuid, name, team, position, overall and birthplace, though ShowZone keeps no secondary positions for that edition; its team ids are named by that edition's codes and teams, which the clubs kept from 2018 to 2021. Checked against Sony's own pages: ShowZone holds the new overall and the team of 113 of the 114 changes of the last roster update (October 30, 2020, in the Wayback Machine); the other is Paolo Espino (a free agent, 55), the one Live card ShowZone lacks. The 95 Live cards whose page Common Crawl (93) or the Wayback Machine (2) captured after that update agree on overall, secondary positions and birthplace.
